I've been working this land for 20 years. I know Quzhou's soil — heavy clay loam, gets hard if you don't manage it. My 8 mu grows wheat in winter and maize in summer on the same ground. That's how my mother farmed it, that's how the whole village does it. I don't need anyone to tell me the schedule.

Some of my children work in the city now, so I do most of the field work myself or with my husband. I can't be too ambitious. I need crops that are reliable and sell well at the local market. I'm not going to experiment much — at my age, a bad harvest hurts the whole family.

**Wheat:** I'll plant in mid-October like always. I'll buy the improved wheat seed from the village seed shop — same kind most neighbors use, probably Jimai 22 or whatever the merchant is pushing this year as reliable. I've learned to base fertilize before planting with compound fertilizer and topdress at jointing. I irrigate 4 times: before sowing to get soil moisture right, once in winter to protect roots from frost, at jointing, and at grain fill. I spray herbicide early and check for aphids before heading. I use the rotary tiller after maize harvest to loosen the soil.

**Maize:** Right after wheat harvest in June I plant maize. No time to waste — the season is short. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or similar, the merchant always has it. I don't till again — just direct seed into the stubble to save my back and save time. I apply fertilizer at planting and topdress at tasseling. I water at seedling, tasseling, and grain fill. My well is reliable so I'm not worried about drought. I spray once for pests, maybe twice if there's army worm pressure.
